key_insight: Three-dimensional DSMC captures measured jet–crossflow interference pressure, while two-dimensional simulations reproduce its structure but overpredict the peak roughly twelvefold.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of reaction-control-jet interference in rarefied hypersonic flow requires resolving three-dimensional kinetic effects.
method: Revisited 1975 DLR helium-jet experiments in Mach 11–12 air crossflow.
Compared 2D and 3D DSMC at three freestream densities spanning Knudsen numbers 0.021–0.125.
Checked planar resolution convergence and plate-alone boundary layers.
evidence_signal: Across all three densities, 3D DSMC matches measured interference-pressure peaks within 25% and peak positions within 3 mm.
watch_item: Both simulation approaches overpredict plate-alone wall pressure by 50–75%, and validation of jet forces over wider Knudsen-number ranges remains ongoing.
paper_title: Kinetic study of Reaction-Control-Jet Interference in Rarefied Hypersonic Crossflow
